title_en: Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave Nintendo Direct — Updating Live
summary_en: Tune in with us for everything announced during today's Nintendo Direct broadcast focused on Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave, live from 7am Pacific / 10am Eastern / 3pm UK time.
body_en:
Tune in with us to find out everything announced in today's Nintendo Direct broadcast focused on Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave , live from 7am Pacific / 10am Eastern / 3pm UK time.
We're expecting 20 minutes of new details for Nintendo's upcoming Switch 2 exclusive, which is set to launch in just over a month on September 17.
Fortune's Weave is the first major launch in Nintendo's beloved RPG franchise for several years, and looks to once again embrace the gameplay that made 2019's Fire Emblem: Three Houses so successful. After a so-so successor in Fire Emblem: Engage, this new title looks to very much be a Three Houses sequel, with the return of Heroes' Relics and Crests, and a familiar face in an older Sothis.
As ever, Fortune's Weave will feature the Fire Emblem series' familiar turn-based gameplay and colorful characters, this time set in and around an enormous arena, site of a championship named the Heroic Games. Join us for all the new details!
Fortune's Weave is set in The Dagda Empire, 1449, and in the capital city of Dagison — a bustling hub, which is where the Heroic Games take place in a Roman-style amphitheature. On offer is a worthy prize: the granting of one wish from Dagda's ruler Solel.
Each of the game's four heroes offer their own storyline and set of allies:
Once a week training is available at the arena. You can also watch battles between your opponents to gather useful intel on their techniques. At the shopping arcade you can enhance your weapons.
A temple will allow you to receive a blessing in battle, which provide stat buffs in battle.
Certification Exams let you try to obtain different classes for your characters.
Townsfolk quests are also available to complete for rewards,
Recruit powerful warriors, who may try and turn you away at first. Luckily, you can try to win them over by giving them gifts or taking them to dinner.
Inns allow you to rest and recharge, and also receive materials automatically over time. It's here that you'll engage in conversations with your support characters.
And from the Pale Raven's Perch you can swap to a different hero, allowing you to play through all four characters in parallel.
Exploration beyond the city of Dagison is possible, with overworld battles and dungeon exploration. But time will pass as you explore, inevitably calling you back to the arena once more.
More to follow...
Tom Phillips is IGN's News Editor. You can reach Tom at tom_phillips@ign.com or find him on Bluesky
